scenes.text: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini. [1] They write essays, code and poems in seconds, but what's actually happening inside? [2] Let's understand large language models, in simple words.
scenes.image: Friendly glowing robot reading a giant stack of books in a futuristic library, flat vector illustration, navy background, violet and amber accents

scenes.text: LLM stands for large language model. [1] It's an AI trained on a huge amount of text, to do one thing really well, predict the next word. [2] It reads billions of pages, [3] learns the patterns of language, [4] and then writes just like a human.

data.definition: An AI trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next word.

scenes.text: Let's play its game. The cat sat on the, what? [1] The model scores every possible next word. Mat is most likely, floor and sofa less so, and moon is almost zero. [2] It picks one, adds it to the sentence, [3] and repeats, word by word. That's how a whole answer appears on your screen.

Isn't that just autocomplete? [1] Your phone keyboard does something similar, but it only learned from your messages. [2] An LLM has read a huge chunk of the internet, trillions of words, and that scale is what makes it feel smart.

So how is an LLM made? In three steps. [1] Pre-training, where it reads trillions of words and learns language and facts. [2] Fine-tuning, where it studies good questions and answers, so it learns to follow instructions. [3] And human feedback, where people rate its answers, so it becomes more helpful and safe.

data.heading: How an LLM is made
steps: Reads trillions of words. Learns language + facts
Studies good Q&A examples. Learns to follow instructions
People rate answers. Gets more helpful + safe

scenes.text: Four words you'll hear everywhere. [1] Parameters are the model's internal knobs, and big models have billions. [2] Training is the learning phase, months on thousands of chips. [3] Inference is using the model, like every time you chat. [4] And the prompt is simply what you type in.

data.heading: Jargon buster
terms: The model's internal knobs. Billions of them.
The learning phase. Months, thousands of chips.
Using the model. Every chat you send.

scenes.text: So where are L L Ms used today? [1] Drafting emails and reports in seconds. [2] Customer support chatbots for banks and airlines. [3] And helping programmers write and fix code.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think L L Ms know everything, and are always right. [2] Not true. They predict likely words, so they can sound confident and still be wrong. That's called a hallucination, so double check important facts.

data.myth: LLMs know everything and are always right.
data.fact: They predict likely words, so they can be confidently wrong. That's a hallucination.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! How does an LLM write its answer? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] It predicts the next word, again and again! It's not searching Google every time.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] An LLM is trained on huge amounts of text. [2] It works by predicting the next word. [3] It's built with pre-training, fine-tuning and human feedback. [4] And it can be confidently wrong, so verify. [5] Next up, tokens and the context window, and why AI forgets things in long chats. Follow AI Maastaaru!
